title: HDP token store
subtitle: UUID reference, read path
What this means: The same store as the content-reference row, with the recipient holding the other reference the implementation writes for every token: the version 4 UUID taken from the token's own header. A UUID binds the token's id and nothing else, so it checks no content. Section 8.2 of the draft calls that a substitution point and steers implementers away from it wherever the resolving party does not control the store. On this board the attacker holds no signing key, so what the reference lets through, the signature catches: the altered token fails hop 1's signature on verify, the forged token and the metadata edit fail the root signature, and the reordered, moved and rolled-back tokens fail because the UUID under which they were found does not match the header they carry. The result is the same six refused and three served as the content-reference row, with two of the six reached by a different check: the altered token and the metadata edit, which the digest refuses on that row and the signature refuses on this one. The tail and middle deletions are served, for the same reason as on that row: a reference resolves to a token or to nothing, and nothing is not an error. The whole-store rollback needs stating rather than scoring, and the draft says so itself: a UUID reference is write-once and names the first snapshot stored, a later extension lives only under its own content digest, so a recipient resolving by UUID sees the earliest snapshot by design, and a rollback of the whole store cannot be told from normal operation. The cell reads served because that is what the read path did; the draft treats it as a property of the reference, which is why it recommends the content reference. Level L0 for the same cumulative reason as the content-reference row.
Where the attacker stands: The attacker holds the store and rewrites entries beneath the TokenStore API, as a backing database, a mounted volume or process memory would allow, so the write-once check in put is not in his way. He holds no signing key.
reproduce_intro: Everything runs offline unless the store is a managed cloud service, in which case the row needs a project of your own. The run seeds a fresh store, applies each edit, confirms it landed, reopens the store and records what came back.
